- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >75% from prior day) — add 3–8% buffer to forecast for rebound.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (days 1–7) — apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean-reversion bias in mid-horizon (days 8–15) — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- Lagged sentiment misalignment — if sentiment peaks 2–3 days before forecast horizon, adjust forecast to reflect delayed reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in low-sentiment periods — if sentiment < 0.1, reduce forecast by 1–4% to avoid underestimating downside risk.
- Horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts often overestimate volatility — cap forecast at 10% above 30-day moving average unless sentiment strongly bullish.
